column2: F96. THE FACTS THAT LIVE IN CODE AND ARE RESTATED IN PROSE.
Tab separated, one fact per line, comments start with a hash.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A fact is written in the code once and then said again in
docs, in rules and in the plan, and the copies go stale silently. Four had. The
solid category list was written as holding three when it holds four and as not
holding Structural Foundations when it does. That one was caught by hand, in a
document a reader would have trusted, and the person who caught it said it was
the same class as the `El` error: a confident statement nobody could check.
IT NAMES FACTS AND NEVER VALIDATES PROSE. A check that tried to read every
sentence is one nobody could keep green, so this one reads the lines that make a
QUANTITY CLAIM or a MEMBERSHIP CLAIM about a named fact, and nothing else. A fact
nobody added is a fact nobody checks, and that is the trade.
THE VALUE IS READ OFF THE CODE AND NEVER OFF THIS FILE. This file says where the
code holds it and where prose repeats it. If it carried the number too it would
be a fifth copy and it would go stale like the other four.
COLUMNS
1  name        what the fact is called, used in the message
2  reader      which reader in check-facts.sh gets the value off the code
3  prose       the files that may restate it, space separated
4  subject     a line is about this fact when it matches this
5  must        that line must also match this, with {V} the value as a digit
and {W} the value as a word, or a dash for no such rule
6  never       that line must NOT match this, or a dash
